title: Tournament page layout
question: Kiln is the look for every option. Pick how the tournament page is arranged, steer one, or re-roll.

options.label: Court map
options.lineage: the venue floor plan pinned at the scorer's table
options.thesis: The page opens on the venue: every court as a tile with what it is playing now and the live score.
options.viewport: Tournament name and stage on an ink band; below it the courts grid (2 per row on a phone), each tile showing court number, teams, score and bracket; pools, playoffs and teams follow in stage order.
options.risk: Before play starts the courts are empty, so draft and check-in lean on the sections below the map.

options.label: Stage track
options.thesis: A stepper across the top (Setup, Pool play, Playoffs, Results) and the current stage's work fills the page.
options.viewport: Name on an ink band, the four-step stage track under it with the current step in ember; the current stage's content below (pool standings in pool play, brackets in playoffs); finished stages fold into one-line summaries.
options.risk: The organizer's settings and team edits move behind the Setup step, one tap further away mid-event.

options.label: Scoreboard first
options.lineage: the results board players crowd around between games
options.thesis: Standings lead: every pool's ranked table (or each bracket's path) at arm's-length size, with organizer tools in a Manage drawer.
options.viewport: Name and stage on an ink band with a Manage button; below, pool standings side by side on a laptop and stacked on a phone, advancing places marked in amber; courts and teams follow.
options.risk: Setup-heavy moments (check-in, confirming settings) live inside the drawer instead of on the page.
